newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's TAM sets sights on U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's TAM sets sights on U.S. market.

text.p: Brazil's regional carrier TAM on Tuesday announced plans to launch new non-stop routes between Brazil and the United States and between major Brazilian state capitals.

Speaking in a news conference TAM president Rolim Adolfo Amaro said the company would begin to offer the new Brazilian flight routes in December, after obtaining approval from the Commercial Air Department, Brazil's air transport agency.
He said flights to the United States would probably begin in the second half of 1997. Amaro refused to say to what U.S. cities TAM planned to fly to.
"An airline can only survive if it's always seeking new ways to increase its market share," Amaro said. "TAM is the first Brazilian regional airline in 20 years to go national."

Amaro said he planned to lease at least six 300-seat planes for TAM's new international air routes; however, he said he was undecided as to whether he would be leasing planes made by Airbus Industrie or Boeing Co.
By expanding to international air travel, TAM will compete head-on with Brazil's largest national carriers Varig, Transbrasil and VASP.
Amaro said the Brazilian domestic and international air transport market had grown dramatically since the successful launch of the Real anti-inflation plan.

Latin America's fastest-growing regional airline, earlier this year TAM acquired the Paraguayan-based Lapsa and expanded its flight routes to include Buenos Aires, Asuncion and Santiago, the capitals of Argentina, Paraguay and Chile.
TAM operates a fleet of 28 Fokker NV Fokker-100 and Amaro said he was in negotiations to lease another 10 planes before the end of the year.
